hooks.text: The full moon does not actually cause crime or emergency room chaos.
Centuries of claims about lunar lunacy are entirely unsupported by data.
Over one hundred studies show zero correlation between the full moon and human behavior.

title: Busting the Lunar Effect Myth
description: Discover why decades of data show the full moon does not control human behavior, crime, or hospital visits.

beats.text: The full moon does not actually cause crime or emergency room chaos.
beats.visual: photograph of the full moon through a telescope, 2020

beats.text: For centuries, people blamed the lunar cycle for spikes in hospital admissions and police calls.
beats.visual: photograph of a hospital emergency entrance at night, 2021

beats.text: Meta-analyses of over one hundred studies show absolutely no correlation with human behavior.
beats.visual: diagram of lunar phases and scientific data analysis, 2022

beats.text: Even the popular twenty-eight day human menstrual cycle is actually a mismatch for the twenty-nine point five day lunar month.
beats.visual: lunar month calendar and biological cycle chart, 2023

beats.text: While the moon pulls on entire oceans, its gravity is far too weak to impact human physiology.
beats.visual: photograph of high tide ocean waves crashing on a beach, 2021

beats.text: Higher tides occur because the Sun, Earth, and Moon align their forces together.
beats.visual: diagram of Sun, Earth, and Moon alignment during spring tide, 2022

beats.text: Coral species sync their spawning with moonlight, but human behavior remains entirely grounded by science.
beats.visual: photograph of coral spawning at night on a reef, 2020

beats.text: Myths about the full moon persist despite the lack of evidence.
beats.visual: photograph of the full moon shining brightly in the night sky, 2021

better_than_last: This episode applies a sharp contradiction hook and a seamless grammatical loop back to the opening claim to maximize view velocity and retention.
